olivia-cse: Customer (AcmeCorp) reports SSO failures immediately after their IdP rotated signing certs. SP rejects SAML response with 'Signature invalid'. Happened ~2026-03-15T08:15Z. Logs + response snippet below, need help triaging.

olivia-cse: Log: `2026-03-15T08:15:21Z auth.saml: validate signature failed: no matching cert thumbprint found`

olivia-cse: SAML KeyInfo snippet from the Response (redacted):
```xml
<ds:Signature>
  <ds:SignedInfo>...</ds:SignedInfo>
  <ds:SignatureValue>...</ds:SignatureValue>
  <ds:KeyInfo>
    <ds:X509Data>
      <ds:X509Certificate>MIIC...OLD_CERT...</ds:X509Certificate>
    </ds:X509Data>
  </ds:KeyInfo>
</ds:Signature>
```

mira-support: Did they publish IdP metadata with both keys? Can you paste the metadata fragment (only KeyDescriptor parts) and the metadata URL so we can fetch/cache? :eyes:

olivia-cse: Metadata URL: `https://idp.acmecorp.com/metadata.xml`
They did include two `<KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\">` entries. The new cert is listed second. SP seems to validate against the first one and fails.

olivia-cse: Curl metadata fragment (sanitized):
```xml
<md:EntityDescriptor entityID=\"https://idp.acmecorp.com/\">
  <md:IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\">
      <ds:KeyInfo><ds:X509Data><ds:X509Certificate>MIIC...OLD_CERT...</ds:X509Certificate></ds:X509Data></ds:KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\">
      <ds:KeyInfo><ds:X509Data><ds:X509Certificate>MIIC...NEW_CERT...</ds:X509Certificate></ds:X509Data></ds:KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </md:IDPSSODescriptor>
</md:EntityDescriptor>
```

raj-eng: Thanks — that pattern explains it. Our SP code picks the first `<KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\">` by default if multiple are present. We do not currently try to match the incoming Response's KeyInfo X509Certificate value to a specific KeyDescriptor before verification.

raj-eng: Quick checks:
- confirm metadata cache TTL on the SP (we cache metadata for 12h by default)
- confirm the IdP didn't remove the old cert from metadata earlier than expected
- check whether the SAML Response KeyInfo contains the full cert (not just a keyName) and no linebreak/whitespace mangling

nora-sre: Workarounds:
- add the new cert to the SP truststore (so both certs are trusted)
- or re-order the KeyDescriptor entries so new cert is first
- or temporarily lower metadata cache TTL on the SP to force refetch (not ideal in prod)

olivia-cse: They overlapped keys but apparently removed the old cert from their internal config ~15m after rotating; SP still had cached metadata with old-first ordering. Customer says they did publish both keys but ordering changed in a subsequent metadata push.

olivia-cse: Repro steps requested by eng:
1) `curl -sS https://idp.acmecorp.com/metadata.xml | xmllint --format -` (inspect `<KeyDescriptor>` order)
2) capture a SAMLResponse from a failed login (`SAMLResponse` base64 decode -> XML)
3) extract `<ds:X509Certificate>` from the Response and compute fingerprint: `echo \"...cert...\" | openssl x509 -inform PEM -noout -fingerprint -sha1`
4) compare against metadata entries and check which one matches

raj-eng: Proposed permanent fix: update SP verification logic to attempt to match the Response KeyInfo X509Certificate to metadata KeyDescriptors first, and fall back to trying any KeyDescriptor that successfully verifies the signature. I'll open a small patch/PR for this behavior. ETA: patch + unit tests within 48h if we can reprioritize.

olivia-cse: Please escalate — customer is P2 (logins failing for multiple users). Can we create an incident and deploy the fallback patch as a quick mitigation? If not deployable, we need to implement the allowlist workaround in the config for this tenant immediately.

sso-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0347 (P2) by olivia-cse. Tags: saml, idp-rotation, auth-outage.

nora-sre: I'll apply a tenant-level override to accept both fingerprints for AcmeCorp and bump metadata cache TTL to 30s for that tenant while we patch. Posting the config change in the next message.

olivia-cse: Thanks — will inform customer and ask them to re-run login flows. Also filing a support note with the repro steps and the temporary allowlist change so it's auditable. :white_check_mark:
